title: Seats in a Row Without Quarrels

concept.title: Check the new neighbour at the moment of seating
body: `n` people sit in a row, and some pairs of people are enemies: they must not sit **next to each other**. Count the ways to seat everybody. This is the permutation search, but with a rule about two **neighbouring** choices: a new person may be placed next to the last seated person only if they are not enemies.

The function remembers only `last`, the person seated most recently, because the rule involves only two neighbours. Since the rule is checked before a person is placed, no arrangement with a quarrel is ever completed. With many enemy pairs the number of arrangements falls quickly; with no pairs it is `n!`.

statement: `n` people, numbered 1 to `n`, sit in a row. `m` pairs of people are enemies and must not sit next to each other. Count the different ways to seat the people in the `n` places.
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two people who are enemies.
constraints: 0 <= m <= n * (n - 1) / 2, every pair appears at most once

examples.note: The six orders are 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, 321; 1 and 2 are neighbours in 123, 213, 312 and 321, so 2 orders remain: 132 and 231.

hints: Place the people one after the other, remembering the last one.
A person may be placed only if they are not an enemy of the last one.
Count one arrangement when all n people are placed.

solution.complexity: Time O(n!) in the worst case (8! = 40320 leaves), space O(n).
